question_html: What is the fixed value of a share printed on the share certificate called?

options.A: Market value
options.B: Nominal, par, or face value[cite: 12]
options.C: Issue price
options.D: Book value

answer_html: Answer: (B) The fixed value of a share, printed on the share certificate, is called nominal, par, or face value of a share[cite: 12].

question_html: Which capital category puts a legal limit on the amount of capital that a company is authorised to raise during its lifetime as stated in the Memorandum of Association?

options.A: Issued Capital
options.B: Subscribed Capital
options.C: Authorised Share Capital or Nominal Capital[cite: 12]
options.D: Reserve Capital

answer_html: Answer: (C) Authorised Share Capital or Nominal Capital is mentioned in the Capital Clause of the Memorandum of Association and limits the capital a company can raise during its lifetime[cite: 12].

question_html: Under Section 65 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is 'Reserve Capital'?

options.A: Profits set aside out of capital profits not available for dividend.
options.B: A portion of uncalled subscribed capital that shall not be called up except in the event of winding up of the company[cite: 12].
options.C: The portion of issued capital subscribed by promoters only.
options.D: A reserve created out of share premium to write off preliminary expenses.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Reserve capital is a portion of uncalled subscribed capital which a company decides by special resolution to call up only in the event of liquidation[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the key difference between Reserve Capital and Capital Reserve?

options.A: Reserve capital is part of uncalled capital, whereas capital reserve is created out of capital profits[cite: 12].
options.B: Reserve capital is shown under reserves and surplus, while capital reserve is uncalled capital.
options.C: There is no difference; both terms are legally identical.
options.D: Reserve capital is available for dividend distribution, whereas capital reserve is not.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Reserve capital is a portion of uncalled capital called up on winding up, whereas capital reserve is part of reserves and surplus created out of capital profits[cite: 12].

question_html: Under Section 53 of the Companies Act, 2013, a company cannot issue shares at a discount except in the case of:

options.A: Right issue to existing shareholders
options.B: Sweat equity shares issued to employees or directors[cite: 12]
options.C: Bonus shares issued to promoters
options.D: Shares issued to financial institutions during debt restructuring

answer_html: Answer: (B) According to Section 53, a company cannot issue shares at a discount except for sweat equity shares issued to employees or directors[cite: 12].
topic_text: Issue of Shares at Discount and Sweat Equity

question_html: What is the minimum percentage of nominal value that application money must represent as per Section 39 of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Not less than 5%[cite: 12]
options.B: Not less than 10%
options.C: Not less than 25%
options.D: Not less than 50%

answer_html: Answer: (A) As per Section 39 of the Companies Act, 2013, application money must be at least 5% of the nominal value of shares[cite: 12].

question_html: According to SEBI guidelines, what is the minimum subscription required to be received in a public issue?

options.A: 50% of the offer through offer document
options.B: 75% of the offer through offer document
options.C: 90% of the offer through offer document[cite: 12]
options.D: 100% (full subscription)

answer_html: Answer: (C) As per SEBI guidelines, minimum subscription shall not be less than ninety percent (90%) of the offer through the offer document[cite: 12].

question_html: In the case of a non-underwritten public issue, within how many days from the closure of the issue must all application moneys be refunded if minimum subscription is not received?

options.A: Within 15 days[cite: 12]
options.B: Within 30 days
options.C: Within 60 days
options.D: Within 70 days

answer_html: Answer: (A) If minimum subscription is not received, application moneys must be refunded within fifteen days of the closure of the issue in case of a non-underwritten issue[cite: 12].
topic_text: Refund of Application Money on Minimum Subscription Failure

question_html: Under Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013, which of the following is an authorized utilization of the Securities Premium Account for companies to which Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) DO NOT apply?

options.A: Writing off any operating losses of the current financial year
options.B: Writing off preliminary expenses of the company[cite: 12]
options.C: Payment of cash dividends to equity shareholders
options.D: Provision for general corporate tax liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (B) Securities premium can be used to write off preliminary expenses for companies not governed by Ind AS[cite: 12].

question_html: What type of preference shares carry the right to receive arrears of dividend accumulated from past years when current profits are insufficient?

options.A: Participating Preference Shares
options.B: Non-cumulative Preference Shares
options.C: Cumulative Preference Shares[cite: 12]
options.D: Redeemable Preference Shares

answer_html: Answer: (C) Cumulative preference shares carry the right to a fixed dividend that accumulates if unpaid due to insufficient profits in current years[cite: 12].

question_html: Under Section 55 of the Companies Act, 2013, what is the maximum period within which preference shares must be redeemed by a company?

options.A: 10 years
options.B: 15 years
options.C: 20 years (except for specified infrastructure projects)[cite: 12]
options.D: 30 years

answer_html: Answer: (C) No company limited by shares shall issue preference shares redeemable after the expiry of 20 years from the date of issue, except for specified infrastructure projects[cite: 12].

question_html: Under what condition are holders of cumulative preference shares entitled to take part and vote on every resolution in general meetings?

options.A: Whenever the company earns net profits exceeding 20%.
options.B: When the dividend on preference shares remains in arrears for a period of not less than two years[cite: 12].
options.C: At the discretion of the Board of Directors every year.
options.D: When the equity dividend exceeds 15%.

answer_html: Answer: (B) In case cumulative preference dividend remains in arrears for a period of not less than two years, holders of such shares are entitled to vote on every resolution[cite: 12].

question_html: According to Table F of the Companies Act, 2013, what are the maximum prescribed rates of interest on 'Calls-in-Arrears' and 'Calls-in-Advance' respectively?

options.A: 12% p.a. and 10% p.a.
options.B: 10% p.a. and 12% p.a.[cite: 12]
options.C: 6% p.a. and 12% p.a.
options.D: 10% p.a. and 15% p.a.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Table F prescribes 10% p.a. for calls in arrears and 12% p.a. for calls in advance as maximum rates[cite: 12].

question_html: When shares are forfeited, how is the Share Capital Account affected in terms of accounting entries?

options.A: Credited with the total face value of issued shares
options.B: Debited with the called-up value of shares forfeited[cite: 12]
options.C: Debited with the amount actually received on shares
options.D: Credited with calls-in-arrears

answer_html: Answer: (B) When shares are forfeited, Share Capital Account is debited with the called-up value of shares forfeited[cite: 12].

question_html: If shares originally issued at a premium are forfeited and the premium has NOT been received from the defaulting shareholder, what entry is passed regarding the Securities Premium Account?

options.A: Securities Premium Account is credited with the premium amount.
options.B: Securities Premium Account is debited to cancel the unreceived premium[cite: 12].
options.C: Securities Premium Account remains unaffected.
options.D: Securities Premium Account is transferred directly to Capital Reserve.

answer_html: Answer: (B) If the premium has not been received, the Securities Premium Account is debited at forfeiture to cancel it[cite: 12].
topic_text: Forfeiture of Shares Issued at Premium

question_html: Can a company cancel the Securities Premium Account if the premium amount has ALREADY been received prior to the forfeiture of shares?

options.A: Yes, it must be refunded to the shareholder upon forfeiture.
options.B: No, if the premium has already been received, it cannot be cancelled even if shares are forfeited[cite: 12].
options.C: Yes, by passing an ordinary resolution in the board meeting.
options.D: Only with the approval of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).

answer_html: Answer: (B) If the premium has already been received by the company, it cannot be cancelled even if the shares are forfeited in the future[cite: 12].
topic_text: Forfeiture of Shares Issued at Premium (Received)

question_html: What is the legal nature of the re-issue of forfeited shares?

options.A: It is a fresh allotment of shares by the company.
options.B: It is merely a sale of forfeited shares by the company[cite: 12].
options.C: It is a conversion of debt into equity instruments.
options.D: It is a bonus issue to existing shareholders.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Reissue of forfeited shares is not an allotment of shares but only a sale[cite: 12].

question_html: Where is the surplus (profit) on the re-issue of forfeited shares transferred upon completion of the re-issue?

options.A: General Reserve Account
options.B: Capital Reserve Account[cite: 12]
options.C: Securities Premium Account
options.D: Statement of Profit and Loss

answer_html: Answer: (B) The profit on re-issue of forfeited shares is transferred to Capital Reserve Account[cite: 12].
topic_text: Transfer of Re-issue Profit to Capital Reserve

question_html: When only a portion of the forfeited shares are re-issued, how should the profit on re-issue be calculated and treated?

options.A: Total forfeiture profit of all forfeited shares is transferred to Capital Reserve.
options.B: Only the profit made on the re-issue of that specific portion of shares is transferred to Capital Reserve[cite: 12].
options.C: No transfer to Capital Reserve is allowed until all forfeited shares are re-issued.
options.D: The entire forfeited amount of unissued shares is transferred to Capital Reserve.

answer_html: Answer: (B) When only a portion of forfeited shares are re-issued, the profit made on re-issue of such portion of shares only must be transferred to Capital Reserve[cite: 12].

question_html: Under Accounting Standards, when an asset is acquired by the issue of shares, what is the acquisition cost recorded as?

options.A: The nominal or par value of the shares issued
options.B: The fair value of the securities issued[cite: 12]
options.C: The historical book value of the asset in the vendor's books
options.D: The market price of the asset determined by court

answer_html: Answer: (B) Under accounting standards, the acquisition cost when shares are issued for non-cash consideration is the fair value of the securities issued[cite: 12].
topic_text: Shares Issued for Consideration Other Than Cash

question_html: What is pro-rata allotment of shares?

options.A: Allotment of shares in proportion to the shares applied for when an issue is over-subscribed[cite: 12].
options.B: Allotment of shares strictly on a first-come, first-served basis.
options.C: Proportional refund of application money without issuing shares.
options.D: Allotment of shares only to institutional investors.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Pro-rata allotment means allotment in proportion of shares applied for when an issue is over-subscribed[cite: 12].

question_html: How is the amount of 'Calls-in-Arrears' presented in the company's Balance Sheet?

options.A: Added to current liabilities
options.B: Deducted from called-up capital to arrive at paid-up value[cite: 12]
options.C: Shown under current assets as receivables
options.D: Ignored until shares are forfeited

answer_html: Answer: (B) Calls-in-arrears represent uncollected capital and are shown by way of deduction from called-up capital to arrive at paid-up share capital[cite: 12].

question_html: What are 'Sweat Equity Shares' defined as?

options.A: Shares issued to the general public at a heavy discount during financial distress.
options.B: Equity shares issued by a company to its directors or employees at a discount or for consideration other than cash for providing know-how or IPR[cite: 12].
options.C: Shares issued exclusively to underwriters as commission.
options.D: Preference shares carrying extra voting rights.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Sweat equity shares are equity shares issued to directors or employees at a discount or for non-cash consideration for know-how or intellectual property rights[cite: 12].

question_html: G Ltd. acquired assets worth ₹7,50,000 from H Ltd. by issuing shares of ₹100 each at a premium of 25%. How many shares were issued?

options.A: 6,000 shares[cite: 12]
options.B: 7,500 shares
options.C: 9,375 shares
options.D: 5,000 shares

answer_html: Answer: (A) Issue price per share = ₹100 + 25% = ₹125. Number of shares = ₹7,50,000 / ₹125 = 6,000 shares[cite: 12].
topic_text: Calculation of Shares Issued for Assets

question_html: Under the Companies Act, 2013, can a company issue irredeemable preference shares?

options.A: Yes, without any restrictions.
options.B: No company limited by shares shall issue irredeemable preference shares[cite: 12].
options.C: Yes, if approved by 75% of equity shareholders.
options.D: Only if listed on a recognised stock exchange.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Companies Act, 2013 prohibits the issue of any preference share which is irredeemable[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the relationship between Authorised Capital and Issued Capital?

options.A: Authorised Capital = Issued Capital + Unissued Capital[cite: 12]
options.B: Issued Capital is always equal to Authorised Capital.
options.C: Authorised Capital is a part of Subscribed Capital.
options.D: Issued Capital cannot exceed 50% of Authorised Capital.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Authorised Capital equals the sum of issued capital and unissued capital[cite: 12].

question_html: What are 'Participating Preference Shares'?

options.A: Shares that confer the right to participate in surplus profits after equity shareholders are paid a stipulated rate[cite: 12].
options.B: Preference shares that carry voting rights in all general meetings without exception.
options.C: Shares that allow participation in the management board.
options.D: Preference shares that can be converted into debentures at the holder's option.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Participating preference shares confer the right to participate in surplus profits and surplus on winding-up after equity shareholders have been paid off[cite: 12].

question_html: When shares are forfeited, what amount is credited to the Forfeited Shares Account?

options.A: The total nominal value of shares forfeited
options.B: The amount already received in respect of those shares[cite: 12]
options.C: The unpaid call amount
options.D: The market value of shares on the date of forfeiture

answer_html: Answer: (B) Forfeited Shares Account is credited with the amount already received in respect of the forfeited shares[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the liability of owners in a company compared to a sole-proprietorship?

options.A: Unlimited in both forms of business
options.B: Limited to the issue price of shares held in a company, whereas unlimited in sole-proprietorship[cite: 12]
options.C: Limited to the paid-up capital in sole-proprietorship and unlimited in a company
options.D: Joint and several for all business debts in a company

answer_html: Answer: (B) Liability of owners in a company is limited to the issue price of shares held, whereas it is unlimited in a sole-proprietorship[cite: 12].

question_html: How is 'Paid-up Share Capital' mathematically related to called-up capital?

options.A: Paid-up capital = Called-up capital + Calls-in-advance - Calls-in-arrears[cite: 12]
options.B: Paid-up capital = Called-up capital - Calls-in-arrears + Calls-in-advance
options.C: Paid-up capital = Called-up capital + Calls-in-arrears
options.D: Paid-up capital = Issued capital - Uncalled capital

answer_html: Answer: (A) Called up capital = Paid up capital + Calls in arrears - Calls in advance, hence Paid-up Capital = Called-up Capital + Calls-in-advance - Calls-in-arrears[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the term used when applications are received for a greater number of shares than those offered by the company?

options.A: Under-subscription
options.B: Full subscription
options.C: Over-subscription[cite: 12]
options.D: Sweat subscription

answer_html: Answer: (C) Over-subscription occurs when applications received are more than shares issued[cite: 12].

question_html: Which account is credited when shares are issued at a price higher than their face value?

options.A: Capital Reserve Account
options.B: Securities Premium Account[cite: 12]
options.C: Share Capital Account
options.D: General Reserve Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) When shares are issued at a premium, the premium amount is credited to Securities Premium Account[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the process through which a company determines its share prices by establishing a price band and receiving investor bids called?

options.A: Underwriting process
options.B: Book building process[cite: 12]
options.C: Pro-rata allotment
options.D: Capitalization of reserves

answer_html: Answer: (B) Book building is a process through which a company determines its share prices by setting a price band and collecting investor bids[cite: 12].

question_html: In the case of an underwritten issue where minimum subscription is not received within the stipulated period, what is the maximum time limit from the closure of the issue for refunding application money?

options.A: 15 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: 70 days[cite: 12]

answer_html: Answer: (D) In an underwritten issue where minimum subscription including devolvement obligations is not received within 60 days, refund must occur within seventy days of the closure of the issue[cite: 12].

question_html: Are preference shares cumulative and participating by default unless stated otherwise?

options.A: Yes, they are always cumulative and participating.
options.B: No, preference shares are cumulative and non-participating unless expressly stated otherwise[cite: 12].
options.C: They are non-cumulative and participating by default.
options.D: They carry no fixed dividend rights unless converted.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Preference shares are cumulative and non-participating unless expressly stated otherwise[cite: 12].

question_html: What happens to the credit balance remaining in the Forfeited Shares Account for shares that have NOT yet been re-issued?

options.A: Transferred immediately to Capital Reserve
options.B: Distributed as interim dividend to shareholders
options.C: Carried forward and shown under 'Share Capital' in the balance sheet[cite: 12]
options.D: Transferred to Securities Premium Account

answer_html: Answer: (C) The forfeited amount on shares not yet re-issued is carried forward and shown under the heading 'Share Capital'[cite: 12].

question_html: What is 'Calls-in-Advance'?

options.A: Amount called by the company but not paid by shareholders
options.B: Portion of capital yet to be called by the company but already paid by a shareholder[cite: 12]
options.C: Application money received before prospectus issue
options.D: Extra premium collected on rights issue

answer_html: Answer: (B) Calls-in-advance is that portion of capital which is yet to be called by the company but has already been paid by a shareholder[cite: 12].

question_html: Can fully paid-up shares be forfeited by a company for reasons other than non-payment of calls?

options.A: No, forfeiture is strictly restricted to unpaid call amounts.
options.B: Yes, fully paid-up shares may be forfeited for realization of debts of the shareholder if the Articles specifically provide it[cite: 12].
options.C: Yes, by passing an ordinary resolution during an annual general meeting.
options.D: Only if ordered by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

answer_html: Answer: (B) Fully paid-up shares may be forfeited for realization of debts of the shareholder if the Articles specifically provide it[cite: 12].

question_html: Do holders of equity shares enjoy a fixed rate of dividend every year?

options.A: Yes, mandated by the Companies Act, 2013.
options.B: No, the rate of dividend on equity shares is recommended by the Board of Directors and may vary from year to year[cite: 12].
options.C: Yes, linked to government bond yields.
options.D: Only if specified in the Memorandum of Association.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The rate of dividend on equity shares is recommended by the Board of Directors and may vary depending on profit availability and dividend policy[cite: 12].

question_html: Within what timeframe must a company produce before the Registrar a written contract of sale or service in respect of which shares have been allotted for consideration other than cash?

options.A: Within 15 days
options.B: Within 30 days
options.C: Within a specified time of allotment[cite: 12]
options.D: Within one financial year

answer_html: Answer: (C) Within specified time of allotment, the company must produce before the Registrar a written contract of sale or service in respect of shares allotted for non-cash consideration[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the limitation on loss when re-issuing forfeited shares?

options.A: Loss on re-issue can be any amount approved by the Board.
options.B: Loss on re-issue should not exceed the forfeited amount (amount originally paid up) on those shares[cite: 12].
options.C: Loss cannot exceed 10% of the face value.
options.D: No loss on re-issue is permitted under company law.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Loss on re-issue should not exceed the forfeited amount so that total amount received is not less than arrears[cite: 12].

question_html: Are shareholders entitled to receive any dividend on calls-in-advance paid by them?

options.A: Yes, at a fixed rate of 12% p.a.
options.B: No, shareholders are not entitled for any dividend on calls in advance[cite: 12].
options.C: Yes, equal to equity dividend rate.
options.D: Only if approved by the stock exchange.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Shareholders are not entitled for any dividend on calls in advance (they receive interest, not dividend)[cite: 12].

question_html: Which companies are prohibited from using the Securities Premium Account to write off preliminary expenses or provide for premium on redemption of preference shares?

options.A: Companies to which Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) are applicable[cite: 12]
options.B: Banking companies governed by RBI
options.C: Government companies where 51% capital is held by the state
options.D: Small companies and One Person Companies

answer_html: Answer: (A) Companies whose financial statements comply with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) can't apply securities premium for writing off preliminary expenses or redemption premium[cite: 12].
topic_text: Ind AS Restrictions on Securities Premium

question_html: What is the accounting nature of Interest on Calls-in-Arrears and Interest on Calls-in-Advance respectively for a company?

options.A: Both are capital receipts.
options.B: Interest on calls in arrears is an income (nominal account), while interest on calls in advance is an expense[cite: 12].
options.C: Both are operating expenses.
options.D: Interest on calls in arrears is an expense, while interest on calls in advance is an income.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on calls in arrears is an income credited to P&L, whereas interest on calls in advance is an expense for the company[cite: 12].

question_html: What are the items taken into account by the Board of Directors when determining the 'minimum subscription' amount to be disclosed in a prospectus?

options.A: Preliminary expenses, commission on shares, cost of fixed assets, working capital requirements, and day-to-day operating expenditures[cite: 12]
options.B: Expected future dividend payouts and general reserves
options.C: Market capitalization and stock exchange listing fees
options.D: Promoter remuneration and foreign exchange fluctuations

answer_html: Answer: (A) Minimum subscription takes into account preliminary expenses, commission, fixed asset costs, working capital requirements, and day-to-day operating expenditures[cite: 12].

question_html: According to SEBI regulations, what is the minimum percentage of the issue price that must be paid by an applicant as application money?

options.A: Not less than 5%
options.B: Not less than 10%
options.C: Not less than 25%[cite: 12]
options.D: Not less than 50%

answer_html: Answer: (C) As per SEBI regulations, minimum application money to be paid shall not be less than 25% of the issue price[cite: 12].

question_html: What happens to the title of a shareholder and the amounts paid to date when their shares are forfeited by the company?

options.A: Title is extinguished and amounts paid to date are refunded.
options.B: Title is extinguished and amounts paid to date are NOT refunded[cite: 12].
options.C: Title remains intact until shares are re-issued at a profit.
options.D: The shareholder retains voting rights for 6 months post-forfeiture.

answer_html: Answer: (B) When shares are forfeited, the title of the shareholder is extinguished and the amount paid to date is not refunded[cite: 12].

question_html: Can directors cancel a share forfeiture before the forfeited shares are re-allotted?

options.A: No, forfeiture is irreversible once resolved.
options.B: Yes, directors have the right to cancel such forfeiture before the forfeited shares are re-allotted[cite: 12].
options.C: Only with the sanction of an extraordinary general meeting.
options.D: Only if the defaulting shareholder pays double the arrears.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Directors also have the right to cancel such forfeiture before the forfeited shares are re-allotted[cite: 12].

question_html: What authority administers matters related to issue and transfer of securities under Section 24 of the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
options.B: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)[cite: 12]
options.C: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
options.D: Registrar of Companies (RoC)

answer_html: Answer: (B) According to Section 24 of the Companies Act, 2013, matters related to issue and transfer of securities will be administered by SEBI[cite: 12].

question_html: What is the period considered for calculating interest on calls-in-arrears and interest on calls-in-advance respectively?

options.A: Calls-in-arrears: due date to final receipt date; Calls-in-advance: receipt date to date call is made due[cite: 12].
options.B: Calls-in-arrears: receipt date to financial year end; Calls-in-advance: due date to redemption date.
options.C: Both are calculated strictly from the beginning of the financial year.
options.D: Calls-in-arrears: date of forfeiture; Calls-in-advance: date of allotment.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Calls-in-arrears interest considers the period from the date call money was due to final receipt date, while calls-in-advance considers from the date money was received to the day call was made due[cite: 12].
